SMTO-FIL-0034 — SMTO couldn't read the original file's details for the copy

GUID: ea225d66-e8bd-4bb6-baef-964f85628b44
Slug: file-invalid-source-receipt
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • When SMTO opened the original file to copy it to another Gateway, that Gateway didn't report a usable size or identity for it. SMTO stopped before sending anything to the destination.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to show the original file's details, such as its size, to confirm it exists and can be read. SMTO needs a valid size for the original file before it can copy it safely.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and use Check for updates on the Gateway that holds the original file. An out-of-date Gateway may describe files in a way this version of SMTO doesn't accept.
  3. Confirm the file isn't already at the destination, then ask SMTO to copy it again. Checking first avoids making a duplicate or replacing a copy that is already there.

What success looks like

  • The copy finishes and SMTO reports the file was copied and verified.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages the Gateway that holds the original file. Don't keep repeating the copy; the same reply will be refused until that Gateway is fixed or updated.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway copy's source_open receipt had a non-integer or negative size_bytes, or a revision that was missing, not 'f1:'-prefixed or longer than 128 characters, so the relay stopped before destination_begin.

What this means

  • The source-open receipt has a non-integer/negative size or missing, malformed or oversized f1 revision. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The source-open receipt has a non-integer/negative size or missing, malformed or oversized f1 revision.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the safe source receipt schema and selected Gateway compatibility before opening destination work.

How to fix it

  • Check the source Gateway's version and log for transfer-protocol drift, and confirm the source path is a regular file whose stat succeeds. No destination stage was opened; start a new copy only after the source returns a valid size and f1 revision.
  • Refresh the source receipt from the authoritative source through the transfer flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The authoritative source returns a valid current size and revision.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
